text: This closes out the DDL cluster that opened this chapter. Synonyms are a small feature with a real, practical use: a short, stable alias for another database object, wherever it actually lives.

Create synonym dbo dot ShortName for SomeServer dot SomeDatabase dot SomeSchema dot LongObjectName. A synonym points at another object — same database, a different database on the same server, or even a different server through a linked server. Once created, you query it exactly as if it were the real table.

Create synonym dbo dot Products for AdventureWorks2012 dot Production dot Product. Select top 5 Name, ListPrice from dbo dot Products. Every query can now use the short, local, memorable name instead of repeating the full cross-database reference everywhere.

Here's why it matters: if the real table gets migrated or renamed, you'd normally have to find and rewrite every piece of code that referenced it. Drop the synonym, recreate it pointing at the new location — and every query using dbo dot Products keeps working, completely unaware anything moved.
That closes this chapter's DDL cluster. Next up: Primary Keys, the fundamental building block of relational design, and the lesson this whole chapter was already building toward.
